## 01 · First Passage — PhD research: when a random walker first arrives (首达——博士研究：随机游走者何时第一次到达)

https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/research/ · https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/zh/research/

Why one target can show two arrival peaks, and what removes the second: my single-author paper, submitted to Physical Review E (a physics journal).

Why it matters: First-passage times are everywhere a search has to succeed: a molecule finding a receptor, a signal crossing a network, a pest finding a trap (Chapter 07).

_Fig. 1 — A ring, one shortcut, and an arrival time that splits in two._

- 30 Jul 2026 · **Geometry-controlled folds: the double-peak paper** (几何控制的折叠：双峰论文) — Submitted to Physical Review E · Jul 2026. ‘Geometry-controlled folds of first-passage-time bimodality under localized absorption’ was submitted to Physical Review E as a single-author regular article on 30 July 2026. It is the first mathematics paper of the PhD: the geometry of a localized absorber decides whether a second arrival peak exists at all, and the peak is lost through a saddle-node fold — the peak meets a valley and both vanish — at a point that can be computed exactly. Every figure on this site that shows the effect is computed by code written for this site — exact master-equation curves and simulated walkers — not taken from the manuscript. Links: [Research atlas](https://zhouyi-xiaoxiao.github.io/valley-k-small/) · [Reproduction archive](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/delayed-first-passage-peak) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/research/#e-research_fpt-dpma-pre-submitted
- 12 Jun 2026 – 2 Jul 2026 · **Why a second peak appears — and disappears** (第二个峰为何出现，又为何消失) — Completed. The ring’s double peak became a threshold theory. Zoom out until steps blur (the diffusive limit) and the walk becomes Brownian motion — continuous random movement — on an interval, with a sink standing for the shortcut. The first-passage density is a signed mixture of decay modes; a second peak needs at least three. With a central sink, the fold comes at a dimensionless sink strength of about 3.0764; there the peak-to-valley gap closes with exponent 1/2 in time and 3/2 in height. Five independent checks agree, including exact lattice calculations and a random-simulation (Monte Carlo) check with 400,000 walkers. Metrics: Critical strength, symmetric case ≈ 3.0764; Fold exponents 1/2 · 3/2. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/research/#e-research_fpt-dpma-fold-theory
- 8 Sep 2026 – 26 Sep 2026 · **The public reproduction archive: code, proofs and records** (公开复现仓库：代码、证明与数据记录) — Live. Everything behind the fixed-budget paper (a manuscript in preparation) is public and checkable: simulation, analysis and plotting code, machine-readable numerical records, interval-arithmetic certificates (calculations with rigorous error bounds), the Lean 4 proof files (Lean 4 is a proof assistant) and the job records from Isambard 3 (a UK national supercomputer), all pinned by SHA-256 checksums, so a change to any file would show. Five releases went out between 8 and 26 September 2026 as the paper was rebuilt — about 1,466 files in the latest, including 100 Python scripts, 27 Lean files and 1,198 JSON records. Anyone can re-run the numbers without asking. Metrics: Releases 5 (v1.0.0 → v1.3.0); Files in v1.3.0 ≈ 1,466. Links: [Repository](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/prescribed-reaction-time-modes) · [Release v1.3.0](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/prescribed-reaction-time-modes/releases/tag/v1.3.0) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/research/#e-research_fpt-reproduction-releases
- 3 Nov 2025 · **PhD in Engineering Mathematics, University of Bristol** (布里斯托大学工程数学博士研究生) — Ongoing. Role: PhD researcher, University of Bristol, School of Engineering Mathematics and Technology (SEMT). The PhD began on 3 November 2025 in the School of Engineering Mathematics and Technology (SEMT) at the University of Bristol. The subject is first-passage time: how long a random walker takes to reach a target for the first time, and why the distribution of that time can split into two peaks. The work has since broadened to span stochastic processes and the evaluation of AI agents. The random walks moving across this page are the same kind of object the thesis studies. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/research/#e-education_life-phd-start
- 23 Sep 2026 · **Programmable multimodality: the fixed-budget paper** (可编程多峰：固定预算论文) — Manuscript in preparation. ‘Programmable multimodality and saddle-node loss of reaction-time peaks under a fixed catalyst budget’ is a single-author manuscript in preparation. A fixed amount of static catalyst, split into thin stripes along the path of a reacting Brownian pair, programs the reaction-time density: at weak noise each stripe removes a fixed fraction of the arriving pairs — a stick-breaking law — so there is exactly one peak per stripe, and designs with prescribed peak times and weights exist, are locally unique and can be found by Newton’s method. Fixed-width stripes can instead lose a late peak through a saddle-node bifurcation, certified by interval arithmetic in test cases. The finite-dimensional and calculus core is checked in Lean 4; the stochastic parts are proved by hand. Links: [Reproduction archive](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/prescribed-reaction-time-modes) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/research/#r-research_fpt-fixed-budget-paper
- 13 Aug 2026 – 25 Aug 2026 · **Programming the number of peaks** (让峰的个数可以编程) — Completed. For a reacting Brownian pair swept past stripes of catalyst, a first theorem (August 2026) showed that a small enough budget split across m stripes yields exactly m reaction-time peaks. A campaign of about 325 million simulated walkers tested it: all 48 cells of the two-stripe phase diagram gave exactly two peaks, a five-peak demonstration put five peaks at their designed times, and a three-dimensional spot check passed unchanged. An explicit bound on the admissible budget was then sharpened by 692 orders of magnitude, and the finite-dimensional core was formalised in Lean 4 (138 audited declarations, no ‘sorry’). Metrics: Simulated walkers ≈ 325 million; Two-stripe cells exactly bimodal 48 / 48; Bound sharpened by 692 orders of magnitude. Links: [Reproduction archive](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/prescribed-reaction-time-modes) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/research/#r-research_fpt-fixed-budget-theorem-campaign
- 5 Jul 2026 · **46 theorems, checked by machine** (46 条定理，由机器核验) — Completed. The exact algebra of the fold paper — from Chebyshev product identities and the rank-one determinant to the closed-form splitting probability and the minimal three-mode theorem — was formalised in Lean 4, a proof assistant, with its mathlib library: 46 theorems across seven modules, with no ‘sorry’ (Lean’s placeholder for a missing proof) and only Lean’s three standard axioms. Numerical constants and analytic limits were left out of scope on purpose and checked numerically instead. Metrics: Theorems 46; Lean modules 7. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/research/#r-research_fpt-dpma-lean
- 4 Jul 2026 · **An interactive course on my own paper** (为自己的论文做一门交互课) — Completed. To understand the fold paper from the ground up, a single-file offline course was built around it: ten chapters that start from undergraduate analysis and linear algebra, build double-peak intuition from walker histograms, show how negative mode weights create peaks, and end with a slider for the sink’s strength that breaks the saddle-node fold live. Every chapter has self-tests. It is a study tool rather than course material — and the seed of the explainer in this chapter. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/research/#r-research_fpt-dpma-course
- Jul 2026 · **Working paper: spectral diagnostics for encounter–reaction models** (工作论文：相遇-反应模型的谱诊断) — Working paper. A single-author working paper on when two diffusing particles that may react on meeting produce more than one reaction-time peak in finite models. Its tools include a reduction onto the reaction support, a sign-count gate (m peaks need at least 2m − 1 sign changes among the residues), an exact response to redistributing a fixed reactivity budget, and a continuum bridge built from refined two-dimensional lattice ladders and off-lattice Brownian dynamics. The headline conclusion: folds seen on coarse grids escape to the boundary of the admissible region in the continuum. Related work in progress looks at encounters with several reactive zones. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/research/#r-research_fpt-encounter-spectral-paper
- 9 Jun 2026 – 11 Jun 2026 · **The term that cancels** (抵消为零的那一项) — Completed. For a lazy ring with an antipodal shortcut, a ‘t·αᵗ’ term was suspected in the long-time tail of the first-passage distribution. It is not there. Three independent arguments show that its coefficient is identically zero: a partial-fraction sum rule; a trace of the term to an artefact of the generating-function inversion; and symmetry — the transient matrix is diagonalisable, so terms like t·λᵗ cannot occur for any parameters. Every identity was checked in 50-digit arithmetic and with exact rational kernels. Metrics: Independent proofs 3. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/research/#r-research_fpt-secular-term-cancellation
- 28 May 2026 – 31 May 2026 · **Three ingredients of a double peak** (双峰的三个条件) — Completed. A 12-page brief pulled the year’s cases together — ring shortcuts, two-target lattices and exact two-walker encounter searches — and argued that a visible double peak needs three things at once: a balance between the masses of the fast and slow channels, well-separated timescales, and a valley deep enough to resolve. A second talk page on multi-timescale encounters, with a live two-dimensional hopping demo, joined the atlas on 31 May 2026. Links: [Encounter talk page](https://zhouyi-xiaoxiao.github.io/valley-k-small/en/talk/multitimescale-encounter/) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/research/#r-research_fpt-multitimescale-brief
- 15 Apr 2026 · **‘Hidden Routes in First-Passage Time’: a ten-minute talk at the SEMT Ideas Exchange Day** (《首达时间中的隐藏路径》：SEMT 学院「思想交流日」上的十分钟报告) — Deck published. A ten-minute talk for PhD students across SEMT, the School of Engineering Mathematics and Technology, given at its Ideas Exchange Day and built as a web slide deck inside the research atlas, with a live random-walk animation and figures regenerated from the research code. Its one-line thesis: a single target on a ring still produces a fast branch, a valley and a delayed branch once one directed shortcut is present. Deck and script are public in both languages. Metrics: Length 10 min · 9 slides. Links: [Talk (English)](https://zhouyi-xiaoxiao.github.io/valley-k-small/en/talk/smet-phd/) · [Talk (Chinese)](https://zhouyi-xiaoxiao.github.io/valley-k-small/cn/talk/smet-phd/) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/research/#r-research_fpt-hidden-routes-talk
- 30 Mar 2026 · **BAMC 2026, Norwich** (BAMC 2026，诺里奇) — Attended. Attended the British Applied Mathematics Colloquium 2026 at the University of East Anglia in Norwich, which opened on 30 March 2026 — the first national applied-mathematics meeting of the PhD, and a first look at where first-passage questions sit within the wider field. - 25 Feb 2026 · **A public, bilingual research atlas** (公开的中英双语研究图谱) — Live. On 25–26 February 2026 the first-passage line got its own public website: a static research atlas in English and Chinese, with a continuous ‘book’ of eight chapters, a page for every report, a theory section, interactive figures and typeset mathematics. It maps 27 reports and tracks 130 claims back to their evidence. The repository behind it is organised ‘agent-first’ — one command-line tool, guardrail tests and a machine-readable report registry — so that people and AI agents can work on it in the same way. Metrics: Book chapters 8; Mapped reports 27; Tracked claims 130. Links: [Research atlas](https://zhouyi-xiaoxiao.github.io/valley-k-small/) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/research/#r-research_fpt-research-atlas
- Jan 2026 – Jun 2026 · **From rings to two-dimensional lattices** (从环到二维格点) — Completed. In 2026 the question moved from rings to two-dimensional lattices — periodic, rectangular and reflecting domains, a membrane near the target, two competing targets, local bias fields and two-walker encounters. Of the 27 reports in the public research atlas, 13 belong to this lattice family. One finding: a membrane’s permeability mainly adds to the time spent after the crossing, which is why some geometries keep a clear double peak even with minimal bias. Metrics: Lattice reports 13. Links: [All reports](https://zhouyi-xiaoxiao.github.io/valley-k-small/en/reports/) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/research/#r-research_fpt-grid2d-family
- 21 Dec 2025 – 30 Dec 2025 · **Lazy rings with a shortcut: the bilingual reports** (带捷径的懒惰环：中英双语报告) — Completed. The ring studies were consolidated into bilingual reports: a lazy ring with a one-way shortcut, two neighbour kernels, scans over shortcut strength β and ring size N, Monte Carlo trajectory classes and tail diagnostics. The long-time tail turned out to be set by the spectral radius of the transient chain, and β* = 0.01 was the smallest shortcut strength at which both kernels meet the double-peak criterion. A suspicious plateau in one figure was traced to a truncation in the numerical inversion and fixed — the first of many bugs caught by refusing to trust a pretty curve. Links: [Report in the atlas](https://zhouyi-xiaoxiao.github.io/valley-k-small/en/reports/ring_lazy_jump_ext/) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/research/#r-research_fpt-jumpover-ring-reports
- 10 Dec 2025 · **Computing on the Isambard supercomputers** (在 Isambard 超算上计算) — Ongoing. From December 2025 the heavy computation ran on Isambard, the UK national AI supercomputers hosted in Bristol, as part of a university project on random walkers in disordered environments. Command-line automation syncs the code, submits jobs to the scheduler and fetches the results. Isambard-AI carried the encounter paper’s heavy runs from the lattice to the continuum limit — lattice ladders refined up to n = 33 and Brownian dynamics with 20 million walkers per release position — and Isambard 3 ran the large-scale checks for the fixed-budget paper in September 2026, including a census of 2 billion walkers. Metrics: Walkers in one census 2 billion. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/research/#r-research_fpt-isambard-hpc
- 28 Nov 2025 · **First PhD code: a ring with defects** (博士第一份代码：带缺陷的环) — Completed. Within four weeks of starting, a first prototype was specified and built: a Python simulation of a random walk on a one-dimensional ring with defects, with analysis scripts, parameter scans and a small web visualiser. One configuration already hinted at a two-humped first-passage histogram. It was a sketch rather than a result, and it was archived once the exact methods arrived — but it is the baby picture of the whole research line. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/research/#r-research_fpt-rw-defects-prototype
- Sep 2024 – Sep 2025 · **MSc research: first passage in confined random walks** (硕士研究：受限随机游走中的首达现象) — Completed. The MSc in Engineering Mathematics at Bristol (2024–25) finished with a Distinction (the top UK grade) and a dissertation titled ‘First-Passage Phenomena in Confined Random Walks: Finite-Size Effects, Exact Solutions, and Spatial Heterogeneity’. It asked how long a random walker takes to first reach a target on one-, two- and three-dimensional lattices, with and without defects, and set exact solutions against simulation. The code is public. It is the first place the walker got trapped in a box — and the question has not let go since. Metrics: Classification Distinction. Links: [Article (2026): paper, proofs, code](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/master-dissertation) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/research/#r-research_fpt-msc-dissertation

## 02 · Skipping the IME? — First AI paper · UKAIRS 2026, the UK AI Research Symposium (跳过输入法？——第一篇 AI 论文 · 英国 AI 研究研讨会（UKAIRS 2026）)

https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/ai/skipping-the-ime/ · https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/zh/ai/skipping-the-ime/

Pinyin (romanised Chinese) alone? Edinburgh poster, 48 exploratory runs: everyday instructions worked; proper names and homophones needed characters.

Why it matters: Many languages are typed through an input method — software that turns typed letters into characters — or a romanisation: pinyin (romanised Chinese), Japanese romaji, Arabizi. Knowing where meaning survives the shortcut tells people when they can skip that step with an AI agent.

_Fig. 2 — Toneless pinyin as a walk that can end at the wrong word._

- 31 May 2026 · **The key finding: toneless pinyin erases homophones** (核心发现：无声调拼音抹掉同音字) — Completed. Three adversarial tasks hinge on words that collapse without tones: shu alone is 书 ‘book’, 树 ‘tree’, 输 ‘lose’ and 熟 ‘ripe’. In this exploratory test, native characters scored 1.00, and so did the mixed workflow — instructions in pinyin, critical terms in characters. Clean, unspaced and misspelt pinyin all averaged 0.333: the agent left the answer in pinyin or picked the wrong character. The one task that survived, 买 ‘buy’ against 卖 ‘sell’, was saved by 入 ‘in’ and 出 ‘out’. An uncalibrated estimate puts the mixed prompt at 0.82 of the input-method keystrokes; typing effort was not measured. Metrics: Native characters · mixed 1.00 · 1.00; Pinyin only (clean, no-space, typo) 0.333. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/ai/skipping-the-ime/#e-ai_research-phase4-homophone
- 11 Aug 2026 · **UKAIRS 2026: first-author paper accepted as a poster** (UKAIRS 2026：第一作者论文录用为海报) — Accepted. On 11 August 2026 UKAIRS accepted the paper for a poster session in the Emerging Research track. The reviews found the question genuinely interesting, the tool potentially useful and the inclusivity angle worth pursuing, and recommended leading with the ‘shi shi’ example and the three-layer analysis — encoding change, compression, tone loss. It is my first peer-reviewed AI paper, and I am first author. Links: [Poster list](https://ukairs2026.eventsadmin.com/i/PosterSessions) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/ai/skipping-the-ime/#e-ai_research-ukairs-acceptance
- 24 Nov 2026 – 25 Nov 2026 · **UK AI Research Symposium (UKAIRS 2026), Edinburgh** (英国 AI 研究研讨会（UKAIRS 2026），爱丁堡) — Poster · 25 Nov 2026. UKAIRS 2026, the UK AI Research Symposium: 24–25 November 2026, John McIntyre Conference Centre, Edinburgh; poster #181 in the poster session of Wednesday 25 November, 13:15–14:15. The plan, written into the paper, is a side-by-side demo — the native prompt, its keyboard-friendly variant, the agent’s response, the grade and the effort estimate — so that visitors can toggle from routine prompts to homophone traps and watch where meaning collapses. Chapter 02 of this site is an early version of that demo. Links: [Poster list](https://ukairs2026.eventsadmin.com/i/PosterSessions) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/ai/skipping-the-ime/#e-ai_research-ukairs-presentation
- 12 Dec 2026 · **NeurIPS 2026 Fusion Equilibrium Challenge: second place in Challenge 1 and an invited talk** (NeurIPS 2026 聚变平衡挑战赛：挑战一第二名与受邀报告) — Invited talk · 12 Dec 2026. The Fusion Equilibrium Challenge, in the NeurIPS 2026 Competition Track, asks for the magnetic flux map of a tokamak (a fusion device) to be predicted from its coil currents and Thomson-scattering profiles (laser measurements of the plasma), without magnetic sensors. In the blind Final, with results announced on 14 November 2026, the solo entry took second place in Challenge 1, on DIII-D, with a score of 0.997253, and 13th place in Challenge 2, zero-shot transfer to MAST. The invited 15-minute talk at the competition workshop in Atlanta on 12 December 2026 is an interactive web page rather than slides. The code is public under the MIT licence. Metrics: Challenge 1 score 0.997253. Links: [Interactive talk page](https://fusion.zhouyixiaoxiao.com) · [Code (MIT licence)](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/fusion-equilibrium-challenge-2026) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/ai/skipping-the-ime/#e-ai_research-fusion-challenge
- 25 Feb 2026 · **An AI-native way of doing mathematics** (一种 AI 原生的做数学方式) — Ongoing. Across the first-passage line a repeatable loop took shape: AI models propose derivations and code, separate agents attack the claims, numerical computation acts as the arbiter, and exact algebra is machine-checked in Lean 4, a proof assistant. The documented cases include proposed formulas that failed numerical checks and were discarded, a repository-grounded audit that caught errors an outside model could not see, and multi-round reviews — up to about sixty agents in a single audit — before each submission. The principle in one line: AI can generate more scientific possibilities; the research skill is deciding which ones deserve belief. Metrics: Agents in one audit ≈ 60; Lean-checked theorems (fold paper) 46. Links: [Research atlas](https://zhouyi-xiaoxiao.github.io/valley-k-small/) · [Reproduction archive (first-passage work)](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/prescribed-reaction-time-modes) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/ai/skipping-the-ime/#e-research_fpt-ai-native-research-method

- 11 Aug 2026 · **What the next version will measure** (下一版要测什么) — Planned. The next study will measure typing effort and answer quality together, with a small typing experiment instead of a keystroke model; add about thirty homophone tasks with graded ambiguity; record the exact version of every model; and test why normalising the input first can lower quality. Claims will stay within the languages and tasks actually tested — the eight-language harness is built for the broader test. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/ai/skipping-the-ime/#r-ai_research-ime-eval-v2-roadmap
- 30 Jun 2026 – 1 Jul 2026 · **Triangulated audit: three minds and a calculator** (三角审计：三个大脑加一台计算器) — Shipped. A reusable audit skill that attacks a research package from three angles over several rounds — a multi-agent workflow with access to the repository and tools, a strong external model, and a numerical and empirical arbiter — and settles every disagreement between models by computation rather than authority. The audit that motivated it showed why: a strong external model got a formula and a threshold wrong that the other participants got right; only the union plus the arbiter was complete; and a mistaken refutation forced a certification that made the result stronger. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/ai/skipping-the-ime/#r-ai_research-triangulated-audit
- 9 Jun 2026 · **Scaling to eight languages** (扩展到八种语言) — Planned. The next study was built before a single call was spent: 44 tasks across eight languages (264 prompt variants), split into high-risk exact-script tasks and controls; a fixed set of leading models; statistics that estimate uncertainty by resampling paired results; and generators for every table and figure. An adversarial audit from eight native-fluency perspectives replaced four homophone pairs that did not truly collapse. Whether to run the main study is still to be decided, so there are no multilingual results yet — and none are claimed. Metrics: Tasks · languages · variants 44 · 8 · 264. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/ai/skipping-the-ime/#r-ai_research-multilingual-sprint
- 8 Jun 2026 · **A second agent, the same boundary** (换一个智能体，边界依旧) — Completed. Nine real calls to Claude Code on the same three homophone tasks reproduced the pattern exactly: native and mixed prompts scored 1.00, clean pinyin averaged 0.333. The pinyin ‘shi shi jian yan’, for example, came back as 实时检验 (‘real-time check’) for both items, instead of 事实检验 (‘fact check’) and 实施检验 (‘implementation check’). Two earlier batches were excluded as infrastructure failures rather than counted. The check made the finding cross-agent — reported in the paper as a small check, not a model comparison. Metrics: Valid calls 9. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/ai/skipping-the-ime/#r-ai_research-claude-cross-check
- 8 Jun 2026 · **When the tool changes underneath: pin the model** (工具在脚下悄悄变了：钉死模型版本) — Completed. A prepared 48-call boundary study, with a new glossary condition, returned an error on every call. For reproducibility the harness ignored the command-line tool’s user configuration, so it fell back to a built-in default model that the signed-in account could not use. The batch was reported as a failure rather than scored as data; the model was then pinned explicitly and a one-call smoke confirmed the fix. The audit trail surfaced a second lesson: the exact model behind the earlier successful phases had not been recorded. Product tools change underneath you — pin exact model IDs. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/ai/skipping-the-ime/#r-ai_research-phase5-model-drift
- 8 Jun 2026 · **The UKAIRS paper: prompting AI agents in pinyin (romanised Chinese)** (UKAIRS 论文：用拼音向 AI 智能体下指令) — Submitted. ‘Skipping the IME? Keyboard-Friendly Multilingual Prompting for LLM Agents’ went to UKAIRS 2026, the UK AI Research Symposium, on 8 June: a two-page paper in the Emerging Research track, under the theme of synergistic human–AI collaboration, typeset so that the Chinese examples render inside an ACM template. It reports 48 valid text-only zh-CN calls — 39 to Codex and 9 to Claude Code, two AI coding agents — and proposes a design rule: skipping the IME (the input method) may be fine for routine scaffolding, but exact names, domain terms and homophones need native-script anchoring. Authors: Xiaoxiao Zhouyi and Yanzhen Li, University of Bristol. Metrics: Valid calls 48 (Codex 39 + Claude Code 9); Pages 2. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/ai/skipping-the-ime/#r-ai_research-ukairs-submission
- 31 May 2026 · **Six input shapes: a ceiling, then a cliff** (六种写法：先撞天花板，再遇悬崖) — Completed. An arithmetic task came back correct under all six input shapes — good evidence that the plumbing worked, but a saturated test. A constraint-following task discriminated: clean pinyin, pinyin without spaces, pinyin with typos and a mixed prompt with English technical terms all returned the required three-item JSON array (a list format a program can read directly), while pinyin initials recovered the topic but lost the structure and scored 0.333. Under a placeholder keystroke model the initials needed an estimated 0.39 of the native keystrokes: a large estimated saving, and a measured loss in quality. Metrics: Initials on the formatting task 0.333 (native 1.00). On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/ai/skipping-the-ime/#r-ai_research-phase2-curves
- 31 May 2026 · **A negative result: restoring the Chinese first made it worse** (反直觉：先还原成中文，反而更糟) — Completed. A small twelve-call repetition reproduced the lower score for abbreviations: direct answers to pinyin-initial prompts averaged 0.444 against 1.0 for native prompts. A ‘normalise, then answer’ wrapper did not rescue it. The mean fell to 0.333 because the model judged the initials too lossy and declined to answer in all three repetitions — turning confident wrong output into honest abstention. Native prompts were unaffected. It is a negative result, and it stayed in the paper. Metrics: Direct vs normalise-first 0.444 vs 0.333. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/ai/skipping-the-ime/#r-ai_research-phase3-normalize-backfires
- 30 May 2026 · **Catching a silent duplicate** (抓住一个隐形的重复) — Completed. A zero-cost audit of all 24 pilot tasks found that the ‘abbreviation’ condition produced prompts byte-for-byte identical to clean romanisation on three tasks — one Chinese, two Vietnamese — which would have silently wasted real calls. A deterministic, script-aware transform now renders syllable initials for Chinese, Japanese and Korean (so ‘shang dian li’ becomes ‘sdl’), and the variant lock records a digest of every rendered prompt, so that even a code-only change is caught by drift checks. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/ai/skipping-the-ime/#r-ai_research-condition-distinctness-fix
- 29 May 2026 – 30 May 2026 · **Four calls, four bugs, then a perfect score** (四次调用、四处程序错误，然后拿到满分) — Completed. Before any model call was spent, the harness was hardened: leakage-neutral work directories, an environment-gated switch for real runs with a hard cap on calls, preflight checks and deterministic scoring, each reviewed by an independent audit. The first real smoke test took four authorised calls and exposed four invocation bugs — relative schema paths, a blocked input stream and the strict rules of structured output. Once they were fixed, the pipeline answered correctly and scored 1.0. The test suite grew from 47 to 87 along the way. Metrics: Calls to first success 4; Bugs found 4. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/ai/skipping-the-ime/#r-ai_research-ime-eval-first-real-call
- 28 May 2026 · **ime-eval: a harness for keyboard-friendly prompting** (ime-eval：免输入法提示词的评测框架) — Completed. ime-eval is the instrument behind the study. It drives real command-line coding agents rather than raw APIs, pairs every native-script prompt with keyboard-friendly variants — clean pinyin, no spaces, light typos, initials, and mixed prompts that keep key terms in native script — and defines profiles for eight input styles, from Japanese romaji and Vietnamese with few or no diacritics to Hinglish, Arabizi, Russian transliteration, Greeklish and Korean. Hard rules from day one: configurations generated automatically, dry-run by default, results written once, and sandboxes that keep answers from leaking to the agent. Named here, not yet public. Metrics: Input styles configured 8; Pilot prompt variants 144. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/ai/skipping-the-ime/#r-ai_research-ime-eval-scaffold
- 28 May 2026 – 9 Jun 2026 · **A relay of three models, refereed by a human** (三个模型接力，一个人当裁判) — Completed. The study ran as a relay between AI systems. An orchestrating model wrote each phase brief; a coding agent implemented and ran it; a third, independent agent audited readiness before any real call was spent — for the homophone phase it returned ‘safe to run’. Every phase ended with a state-and-decision packet handed back to the orchestrator, and every step was committed to git. The human role was the architect’s: choose the phases, authorise the spend, carry the baton. Metrics: Independent readiness audits 4. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/ai/skipping-the-ime/#r-ai_research-three-agent-relay
- 5 May 2026 – 6 May 2026 · **GOSIM Paris 2026** (GOSIM 巴黎 2026) — Attended. Attended GOSIM Paris 2026, ‘The Agentic AI Convergence’, at Station F, the Paris start-up campus, on 5–6 May. The takeaway, written up afterwards: open-source agent ecosystems are moving away from model showcases toward tool interoperability, model serving, edge deployment, production systems and trustworthy workflows — the same direction the evaluation work was heading. Links: [GOSIM Paris 2026](https://paris2026.gosim.org/) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/ai/skipping-the-ime/#r-gap_4_event_attendance_calendar-gosim-paris-2026
- May 2026 · **A research line that bends toward AI** (研究方向延伸到 AI) — Ongoing. Alongside first-passage research on random walks, the PhD work broadened during 2026 toward AI: evaluating AI agents built on large language models (first, whether they can be instructed in pinyin alone), and using multi-model AI workflows as research instruments — adversarial audits whose disagreements are settled by computation. The habit carries straight over: measure the hidden route, then refuse to believe the number until something independent confirms it. The UKAIRS 2026 acceptance is its first peer-reviewed AI output. Links: [Research note: transmission change or reporting change? (one page, PDF)](https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/notes/transmission-or-reporting.pdf) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/ai/skipping-the-ime/#r-ai_research-direction-toward-ai

## 03 · The Engine Room — R&D Scientist (AI) at Yuexin International, a cloud-communications company (机房——阅信国际 · AI 研发)

https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/work/engine-room/ · https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/zh/work/engine-room/

Since June 2026 I have built five AI systems, all live: a gateway, a governance platform, Feishu connectors, a briefing agent and a staff assistant.

Why it matters: The aim: move the company from trying AI to using it every day — safely, with governance built in, and with a person confirming before anything is sent, shared or approved.

_Fig. 3 — Requests as walkers; governance rules decide where each one stops._

Besides the systems below, the work has included drafting the company’s AI plan in July and serving as lead trainer and technical judge for the operations team’s agent training. - 21 Sep 2026 · **Yuexin Cloud AI Assistant — web and desktop** (阅信云 AI 助手——网页版与桌面版) — Live. In one day, an assistant for company staff was built and launched on the company’s model gateway. Colleagues sign in with Feishu and are provisioned automatically, with a personal monthly quota and self-serve API keys. The web app streams its answers, folds away the model’s reasoning, renders Markdown and maths, accepts images and has light and dark themes; a Windows desktop client shipped alongside it, with a download page. Before release it went through three parallel security reviews and an independent review by a second model. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/work/engine-room/#e-company_products-yuexin-chat-launch
- 10 Jun 2026 – 13 Jun 2026 · **An internal AI gateway with Feishu sign-in** (带飞书单点登录的内部 AI 网关) — Live. Within four days an open-source gateway for large language models (LLMs) became the company’s internal AI platform, the Yuexin Intelligent Open Platform. The gateway was chosen by reading the source code of two candidates rather than their brochures. The work covered a deployment runbook, white-labelling and full Chinese localisation of the admin interface, a mobile layout, and a self-service portal where colleagues sign in with Feishu (also known as Lark, a workplace chat-and-docs suite), get a key and see their own usage. Router retries, fallbacks and per-member budgets followed, and a pre-launch audit of model and permission boundaries closed the week. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/work/engine-room/#e-company_products-open-platform-launch
- 25 Jul 2026 – 31 Jul 2026 · **A unified AI access and governance platform** (企业 AI 统一接入与治理平台) — Live. The company’s unified AI access and governance platform went from local build to live in a week, launching on 31 July 2026. It is a self-built portal over an open-source gateway: keys issued by organisation and team, a list of allowed models, budgets and usage, a data-loss-prevention check, and an audit log kept as a hash chain, so that tampering with earlier entries can be detected; the gateway’s own admin interface is closed to the internet. Around launch it went through three kinds of check: several rounds of adversarial review by parallel AI agents; privacy ‘canary’ checks that planted synthetic identifiers and confirmed none survived in storage or logs; and formal production acceptance, with a receipt for every model. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/work/engine-room/#e-company_products-governance-platform-live
- 1 Jun 2026 · **Feishu connectors for AI agents** (飞书连接器：让智能体进入工作台) — Live. A suite of MCP connectors (MCP is an open protocol that lets AI call outside tools) that lets coding agents work inside the company’s workspace in Feishu (also known as Lark, a workplace chat-and-docs suite) — documents, sheets, chats, meeting minutes and approvals — with scoped permissions, acting as the signed-in person rather than as an all-powerful bot. Written documentation made it something colleagues could install, not just a demo. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/work/engine-room/#e-company_products-feishu-agent-connector

The desktop client that shipped with the assistant is being rebuilt as a coding and office agent: an open-source agent engine underneath, a Yuexin interface on top. Planned for the next rounds: a built-in browser and terminal, scheduled tasks, skills, and acting in Feishu, the company’s workplace suite, on the person’s behalf — with a confirmation before every send, share or approval. It is still in development; these are plans, not shipped features. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/work/engine-room/#r-company_products-yuexin-chat-desktop-agent
- 22 Jul 2026 · **A morning briefing written by an agent** (由智能体撰写的晨报) — Live. A daily agent that turns official public procurement notices into leads: it reads each notice, pulls out what is being bought and what is required, and writes a brief that a person can follow up. Everything with consequences — registering, buying documents, pricing, submitting — stays with people. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/work/engine-room/#r-company_products-tender-intelligence
- 14 Jul 2026 – 22 Jul 2026 · **A drafted plan to bring the AI pilots together** (起草方案：收拢零散的 AI 试点) — Plan drafted. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/work/engine-room/#r-company_products-ai-transformation-lead
- 25 May 2026 – 29 May 2026 · **A thesis: communication as AI’s execution layer** (一个论断：通信是 AI 智能体的执行层) — Completed. In May 2026, in a series of memos and one-pagers, an argument took shape: communication becomes the execution layer for AI agents. An agent that can reach people through the channels they already use — messages, notifications — is an agent that can finish a job. It is a personal thesis rather than company strategy, and it explains why a first-passage mathematician ended up building AI systems inside a cloud-communications company whose core business is SMS. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/work/engine-room/#r-company_products-agent-comms-thesis
- 11 Mar 2026 – 21 Mar 2026 · **A Chinese SMS classifier that runs on the device** (在设备上运行的中文短信分类模型) — Completed. An on-device classifier for Chinese SMS, built for a cloud-communications company: a large language model acted as the teacher, labelling examples, and its judgement was distilled into a lightweight student that sorts each message into verification codes, notifications or marketing in well under a millisecond. Three student models were compared on a labelled test set; a support-vector machine (a classic, lightweight classifier) won, with a macro-F1 of 0.91 (an average score that weights every category equally). Fraud detection was deliberately left out of scope. Metrics: Macro-F1 (class-averaged score) 0.91. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/work/engine-room/#r-company_products-sms-classifier

An in-person AI fundamentals session for technical and business staff on 5 August 2026 (the recording runs to 93 minutes) that used the SMS business as a lens on how the large-language-model industry works: a Chinese SMS is billed per 70 characters (67 per segment once a message runs long), a model per token (the unit of text a model reads and writes; depending on the model, one Chinese character can be less than a token or more than one), so the team’s habit of counting characters carries over once that conversion is learned. It ran from the value chain and the cost of tokens to retrieval (looking things up before answering), agents (AI that does tasks for you), hallucination (confident invention) and private deployment (running on your own servers) — and the six questions customers always ask. The materials — a 24-slide deck, a script for a 60-minute version and a handbook with an 81-term glossary, self-tests and customer-dialogue drills — were finalised the next day. Metrics: Length 93 min. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/work/on-stage/#e-company_design_events-llm-industry-training-talk

- 3 Aug 2026 – 16 Sep 2026 · **‘The Confident Assistant’: an AI-literacy escape-room concept** (「自信满满的助手」：一个 AI 素养密室逃脱构想) — Concept. A concept for an AI and programming literacy escape room: an overconfident assistant hands the players code that looks right, and the only way out is to verify it — write the failing test, find the evidence — instead of trusting a confident answer. It is the verify-everything habit of the research, turned into a game for students. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/campus/teaching/#r-ai_research-ai-escape-room

## 06 · Representing — PhD student rep & open-day ambassador (学生代表——博士生代表与开放日学生大使)

https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/campus/representing/ · https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/zh/campus/representing/

I am the Engineering Mathematics PhD rep for a second year; I have sat on a scholarship panel, worked open days — and done seven minutes of stand-up.

Why it matters: Most of what makes a PhD harder is small and fixable — once someone collects it and carries it to the room where decisions are made.

_Fig. 6 — A student’s point, travelling upward until it turns into a decision._

## 07 · Map in. Traps out. — BioPath · Early Career Enterprise Fellow 2026 (one of 12) · New Enterprise: Growth stage (按图布点——BioPath · 2026 年早期职业创业学者（同届 12 人）· New Enterprise：Growth 阶段)

https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/enterprise/ · https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/zh/enterprise/

My prototype BioPath uses first-passage maths to place traps on farms and in grain stores to cut rodenticide use. Early Career Enterprise Fellow 2026.

Why it matters: Where traps go is still largely a judgement call; placing them well could mean fewer chemical rodenticides.

_Fig. 7 — Where to put three traps so that a wandering pest reaches one soonest._

- 23 Dec 2025 · **Early Career Enterprise Fellow, 2026** (2026 年早期职业创业学者) — Awarded. Role: Early Career Enterprise Fellow (2026 cohort, one of twelve), University of Bristol. The application, on 11 December 2025, proposed turning first-passage research into trap-placement software. On 23 December it won one of twelve places in the University of Bristol’s 2026 Early Career Enterprise Fellowship. Metrics: Fellows in the 2026 cohort 12. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/enterprise/#e-school_teaching_service-ecef-awarded
- 23 Feb 2026 · **The BioPath platform: map in, traps out, proof attached** (BioPath 平台：地图进，布点出，附证明) — Live. The software behind the fellowship: a Python platform with a command-line tool, an API and a static site with a demo that runs in the browser. It takes a site map and a monitoring budget and returns trap or sensor coordinates chosen so that a wandering pest is as likely as possible to be caught within a set time, together with an evidence bundle anyone can re-run (the repository calls it the proof bundle) — the optimised score against heuristic and random baselines, the worst-case score across stress-test scenarios and the Monte Carlo runs behind them. The maps in the repository are synthetic demos, and the project site is live. Links: [Project site](https://zhouyi-xiaoxiao.github.io/biopath-platform/) · [Repository](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/biopath-platform) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/enterprise/#e-projects_code-biopath-platform
- 10 Jun 2026 · **A PechaKucha (20 slides, 20 seconds each) at the Festival of Enterprise** (创业节上的 PechaKucha 路演) — Presented. Presented BioPath as a PechaKucha at the University of Bristol Festival of Enterprise in the Arts Complex on 10 June 2026, with a printed poster for the showcase and a one-line promise: ‘Map in. Traps out. Proof attached.’ The talk was also built as a web deck, and that same night it became a subtitled pitch video (now on WeChat Channels). For the fellowship showcase three weeks later, a five-minute pre-recorded version followed. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/enterprise/#e-school_teaching_service-festival-of-enterprise-2026
- 21 Sep 2026 · **‘From strawberry patch to PhD’** (「从草莓田到博士」) — Published. The University of Bristol Careers Service published a Student Founder Spotlight on 21 September 2026 — ‘From strawberry patch to PhD: how engineering maths inspired BioPath’ — on a PhD researcher in Engineering Mathematics building a trap-placement optimisation tool for pest control, and on the route through New Enterprise and the Early Career Enterprise Fellowship to the Festival of Enterprise. Links: [Careers blog](https://universityofbristolcareers.blogs.bristol.ac.uk/2026/09/21/from-strawberry-patch-to-phd-how-engineering-maths-inspired-biopath/) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/enterprise/#e-school_teaching_service-careers-blog-feature

## 08 · Signal — Media, posts and video (信号——自媒体、帖子与视频)

https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/media/ · https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/zh/media/

What I have published: WeChat videos and referenced articles, LinkedIn as a notebook, bilingual subtitles, this site.

Why it matters: Work that no one sees has not quite arrived: posts, talks and videos, in two languages, are how it reaches people.

_Fig. 8 — Three years of a camera roll, month by month: the busy stretches and the quiet ones._

- 29 Aug 2026 · **A WeChat content studio** (微信内容工作室) — Launched. It publishes to WeChat Channels (WeChat’s short-video feed) and a WeChat Official Account (its long-form channel). In October and November 2026 they carried four to-camera videos and long-form articles: figures are checked before they go in, and the sources are listed at the end. A scan of the archive that could pause and pick up again covered 3,943 of the 3,947 videos and found speech in 1,052 — and only such counts are ever published. The channel’s name is 周易潇潇. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/media/#e-self_media-wechat-studio-kickoff
- 10 Jun 2026 – 27 Aug 2026 · **A home-built bilingual subtitle pipeline** (自己搭的中英双语字幕流水线) — Shipped. The local build of ffmpeg shipped without a subtitle renderer, so subtitles took another route: every bilingual cue is rendered as a transparent image and overlaid, in chunks of about ninety seconds processed in parallel, so an 8 min 44 s 4K clip renders in about two and a half minutes. A native Swift tool followed in July, and caption rules in August: at most two lines, 18 Chinese or 46 English characters per line, zero overlaps, and a terminology audit. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/media/#e-self_media-bilingual-subtitle-engine
- Sep 2023 – Aug 2026 · **A camera roll as a diary: 3,947 videos** (把相机胶卷当日记：3947 段视频) — Completed. An inventory of the personal camera roll in August 2026 counted 3,947 videos shot between 3 September 2023 and 27 August 2026 — 140 in 2023, 1,310 in 2024, 1,574 in 2025 and 923 in 2026 up to August. Month by month, the counts show quiet stretches and clear peaks. Only these aggregates are published; the clips themselves stay private. They are the raw material for the WeChat studio. Metrics: Videos 3,947; By year (2023 · 2024 · 2025 · 2026) 140 · 1,310 · 1,574 · 923. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/media/#e-self_media-camera-roll-corpus
- 28 Sep 2026 · **This site: So far.** (本站：至此) — Live. The site you are reading draws the record as a first-passage process, the mathematics of the PhD: random walkers leave Tianjin and stop when they first reach an item, on a timeline from 2021 to now, that matches what you search for. It replaces the page that, since April 2026, simply forwarded zhouyixiaoxiao.com to LinkedIn. It was designed to one written specification and built with AI coding agents; every fact comes from a verified, privacy-tagged record, and nothing private shipped. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/media/#e-prior_site_design-brief-2026-09-28

- 25 Jul 2023 – 20 Sep 2024 · **Five headlines in fourteen months** (十四个月，五个头衔) — Completed. LinkedIn’s email footers keep a quiet record of the profile’s one-line headline: ‘student in Tianjin University’ in July 2023; a day later, ‘Applied Math Student @Tianjin University // Transforming Complexity into Simplicity’; then the same with a line seeking UK summer internships; then back to the plain applied-maths student; and from 20 September 2024, ‘Engineering Mathematics Student @University of Bristol’. That last one has not changed since — not for the PhD, the fellowship or the company role. This site is, in part, the overdue headline update. Links: [LinkedIn profile](https://www.linkedin.com/in/zhouyixiaoxiao/) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/media/#r-gap_1_linkedin_full_profile-account-and-headline-history
- May 2023 · **Light painting, 2023** (光绘，2023) — Completed. In May 2023 a portfolio of light-painting photographs came together: long exposures in which a moving light draws paths that accumulate on the sensor over several seconds. It is the direct ancestor of this site’s central image — a dark plate on which the paths of thousands of walkers accumulate into light. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/media/#r-us_ai_internship_career-light-painting-portfolio-2023

## 09 · Westward — Silicon Valley, 2025 · an internship at LiveX AI, a Bay Area AI start-up (向西——2025 年夏 · 硅谷 AI 创业公司 LiveX AI 实习)

https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/westward/ · https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/zh/westward/

Summer 2025 in Silicon Valley: an entrepreneurship programme and a research internship at LiveX AI (4–16 Aug) — where my turn toward AI began.

Why it matters: It is where the question behind the later AI work first appeared: judge a tool by whether its output answers real questions, not by how it looks.

_Fig. 9 — This walker has not reached its target yet._

- 4 Aug 2025 – 16 Aug 2025 · **Researcher (Internship) at LiveX AI** (LiveX AI 研究实习) — Completed. Role: Researcher (Internship), LiveX AI, a Bay Area AI start-up. LiveX AI, a Bay Area AI start-up, helps consumer companies use AI for customer support, retention and growth. The work ran from a survey of document parsers and a six-dimension quality rubric to a vendor compliance matrix for the engineering team, and ended in a benchmark that checks whether each parser’s output can actually answer questions. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/westward/#e-us_ai_internship_career-livex-ai-internship-2025
- 24 Jul 2025 – 16 Aug 2025 · **Silicon Valley Entrepreneurship Program** (硅谷创业项目) — Completed. About three weeks in the Bay Area on Tianjin University’s Silicon Valley Entrepreneurship Program — a ‘Stanford & Silicon Valley’ programme run with Founders Space, a San Francisco venture builder, for a cohort of about twenty students. I came straight from the Hong Kong camp, and the weeks filled up with a design-thinking workshop, visits to Silicon Valley companies, a symposium at Stanford and evening founder-and-investor meetups — and, inside the same window, a research internship at LiveX AI. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/westward/#e-us_ai_internship_career-silicon-valley-study-programme-2025
- 11 Aug 2025 – 16 Aug 2025 · **LiveX AI internship: a retrieval-QA benchmark for document parsers** (LiveX AI 实习：文档解析器的检索问答评测基准) — Shipped. The internship’s study became a benchmark in its final week, once the engineering team asked for something it could run. The question behind it: which parser turns product manuals into text an AI assistant can reliably answer questions from? Each parser’s output (plain-text Markdown) is treated as a knowledge base and judged by downstream usefulness rather than visual fidelity: the text is split into passages, the most relevant ones are found, and a model answers only from those passages — it may say ‘not found’. Every answer is scored first by checking for the exact answer, then by a grader following a written scoring guide. Wrong answers given with confidence are tracked separately as overconfidence. Five parsers, nine documents, a hundred questions per document: 900 questions for every parser. Metrics: Parsers × documents × questions 5 × 9 × 100. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/westward/#e-us_ai_internship_career-livex-retrieval-benchmark
- Sep 2025 – Jun 2026 · **After: what the summer set in motion** (之后：这个夏天推动了什么) — ∞ still walking. The summer’s question returns in ime-eval and in a first-author paper accepted as a poster at UKAIRS, the UK AI Research Symposium (Chapter 02). Four months after the summer came BioPath and the enterprise fellowship (Chapter 07); in June 2026 applied AI became a job — R&D Scientist (AI) at Yuexin International, a cloud-communications company (Chapter 03). On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/westward/#r-gap_1_linkedin_full_profile-position-livex-researcher
- 5 Aug 2025 · **A week in: an essay about a ladder in the clouds** (一周之后：关于云中天梯的随笔) — Completed. About a week into the programme came a six-part Chinese reflection of roughly 1,700 characters: a night arrival; the Pacific coast and a quiet Stanford campus; walking into the campuses of the big technology companies; conversations with investors and founders; and dawn over the Alviso salt flats. It ends on motivation — everyone stands on a different rung of a ladder wrapped in cloud, so just take your own next step. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/westward/#r-gap_3_us_internship_origin-reflection-essay
- 5 Aug 2025 – 8 Aug 2025 · **Week one: nine PDFs and a six-dimension rubric** (第一周：九份 PDF 与一套六维量表) — Completed. The first week was a sprint: an investigation note on parsing benchmarks and popular tools, four converters run over nine representative test PDFs the same evening, and a written comparison the next day. When the engineering team asked for numbers and one more tool, a fifth was added, and by the end of the week a first deck scored the leading options from 0 to 10 on six dimensions — structural fidelity, formatting accuracy, special content, cleanliness, ease of post-processing and automation readiness. A follow-up request for something runnable set up the benchmark of week two. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/westward/#r-us_ai_internship_career-livex-tool-survey-first-report
- 27 Jul 2025 – 30 Jul 2025 · **Design thinking: getting lost lights a beacon** (设计思维：迷路即点灯) — Team concept. In the first week on site the cohort took a Stanford-style design-thinking workshop, with the worked example ‘new students feel lost at Stanford’. Group 3’s bilingual write-up turned getting lost into a feature: every wrong turn lights a community beacon and reveals a hidden story. It proposed four ‘bridges’ — E-ink beacon tags for leaving notes, a story-card deck whose AR clues unlock only on site, a sculpture projecting a live heat-map of wandering, and Bluetooth guide beacons carried by senior students — and scored wandering paths as ‘Bravery Points’. A random walk rewarded for wandering: the idea turns up again on this site. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/westward/#r-gap_3_us_internship_origin-group3-getting-lost-concept
- 26 Jul 2025 · **A Saturday at Stanford Memorial Auditorium** (斯坦福纪念礼堂的一个周六) — Attended. The first weekend after landing in San Francisco meant a student ticket for the Saturday session of the Asian American Scholar Forum’s Pioneer Medal Symposium and Ceremony at Stanford Memorial Auditorium, 26 July 2025 — the opening frame of the whole Bay Area chapter. Links: [Asian American Scholar Forum](https://www.aasforum.org/) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/westward/#r-us_ai_internship_career-aasf-pioneer-medal-stanford-2025
- 21 Jul 2025 – 25 Jul 2025 · **HKUST Engineering summer camp** (香港科技大学工学院夏令营) — Selected. Selected for the 2025 Summer Camp for Elite Students (21–25 July) at the School of Engineering of the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST), a camp for prospective research postgraduates that included a visit to the Hong Kong Science Park. The first days in Hong Kong led straight on to the Bay Area — the opening of a three-city summer: Hong Kong, Silicon Valley, Bristol. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/westward/#r-education_life-hkust-engineering-summer-camp-2025

## 10 · Workshop — Side projects (作坊——业余项目)

https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/workshop/ · https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/zh/workshop/

What I built in the gaps, mostly so someone else could move faster: a maths guide, a travel-story app, a cursor tool, an agent bridge.

Why it matters: Small public tools are where new methods get tried first, at a scale where failing is cheap.

_Fig. 10 — A year of building, drawn as a walk across the calendar._

- 19 Apr 2026 – 28 Apr 2026 · **London Cuts** (London Cuts 旅行故事工作室) — Live demo. A creator tool for a single-place trip: photos placed by their own metadata, written stories and AI-generated postcards in six art styles, with public reader pages in three visual modes (Punk, Fashion, Cinema), a map atlas and PDF or PNG export. The live demo tells ‘A Year Around London’ in thirteen stops and ‘A Week in Reykjavík’, and it has entry points for AI agents too: an llms.txt, an OpenAPI description and an MCP endpoint (MCP is an open protocol that lets AI call outside tools). London Cuts is a working name. Links: [Live demo](https://london-cuts.vercel.app) · [Repository](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/london-cuts) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/workshop/#e-projects_code-london-cuts
- 5 Mar 2026 – 9 Mar 2026 · **SocialOS: a local-only social-memory assistant, built in five days** (SocialOS：五天做出的本机社交记忆助手) — Completed. SocialOS turns raw notes, voice memos, screenshots and encounters into structured memory about people and events, reflections on yourself and drafts for each platform, delivered through a publishing queue that a human approves. It runs only on the local machine. It was built for the UK AI Agent Hack in five days, with 1,222 commits between 5 and 9 March 2026 — 1,084 of them tagged ‘[autodev]’: commits made by the automated coding agents set up for that week. The public repository keeps the pitch pack and the evidence. Metrics: Commits in five days 1,222; Made by coding agents 1,084. Links: [Repository](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/openclaw-foundry-socialos) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/workshop/#e-projects_code-socialos
- 22 Jul 2023 · **The Tianjin University maths guide** (天津大学数学学院本科生指北) — Live. Rather than just taking the courses, I wrote a guide to them for the students who come after. Started in July 2023, the Tianjin University maths undergraduate guide gathers what a student needs — a foreword, the core courses, the degree programmes and how to contribute — first as a quick guide with a document library, then as a MkDocs site. It has been served at zhouyixiaoxiao.info since December 2025 and is the oldest thing on this page, still online. Links: [zhouyixiaoxiao.info](https://zhouyixiaoxiao.info/) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/workshop/#e-projects_code-tju-math-guide
- 29 May 2026 – 30 May 2026 · **CatchMouse, rebuilt for Apple Silicon** (为 Apple Silicon 重写的 CatchMouse) — Shipped. A clean Swift rewrite of CatchMouse, an Intel-only utility from 2011: a menu-bar agent that warps the cursor to the left, centre or right display with global hotkeys, cycles between displays, remembers custom hotkeys per monitor, flashes display numbers and offers command-line verbs. It builds a universal app with only the command-line tools and needs no accessibility permission. MIT-licensed. Links: [Repository](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/CatchMouse) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/workshop/#e-projects_code-catchmouse
- 27 Jun 2026 – 29 Jun 2026 · **Pro Agent Bridge** (Pro Agent Bridge 智能体之桥) — In daily use. A local MCP server (MCP is an open protocol that lets AI call outside tools) that turns ChatGPT’s developer mode into a bounded coding and hand-off surface for one repository: reading files, searching, exact edits, git inspection and safe verification commands. It extends the MIT-licensed open-source CodexPro by rebel0789 with hand-off from ChatGPT Pro to Claude Code, an AI coding agent, saved-session capture and hardened polling, and it is still in daily use. Credit where it is due: the foundation is upstream. Links: [Repository](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/pro-agent-bridge) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/workshop/#e-projects_code-pro-agent-bridge
- 22 Sep 2026 · **A legal-career roadmap for Bristol Master of Laws (LLM) students** (给布里斯托法学硕士的法律职业路线图) — Live. A responsive, editorial-style Chinese guide for Bristol Master of Laws (LLM) students planning a legal career back in China in 2026–27: chapter navigation, full-text search, filterable events and recruitment, a four-week practice plan, ten copy-ready templates, dated updates on official AI products and 42 primary sources — with no analytics and no backend. The same editorial language as the housing map: a small shelf of Bristol guides. Links: [The guide](https://zhouyi-xiaoxiao.github.io/bristol-law-career-roadmap/) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/workshop/#r-projects_code-bristol-law-career-roadmap
- 9 Jun 2026 – 10 Jun 2026 · **Seven dead ends and a working ⌘T** (七条死路与一个能用的 ⌘T) — Published. A small Swift helper, about 200 lines, that registers ⌘T only while the ChatGPT Atlas browser is in front and routes it to Claude — switching to an existing tab, duplicating it or opening a new one — through the accessibility interface. The README is the fun part: it documents why seven standard approaches fail, because the browser’s new-tab page is a native view rather than a web page. Links: [Repository](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/atlas-claude-tab) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/workshop/#r-projects_code-atlas-claude-tab
- 26 Apr 2026 – 27 Apr 2026 · **A fashion-editorial housing map** (时装杂志风的租房地图) — Live. A single-page map for incoming Chinese Master of Laws (LLM) students at Bristol: seventeen student housing options within about a twenty-minute walk of the Law School, each tagged by how its information was sourced — verified, provider, search or live — with an application section, a mobile detail panel and an offline basemap fallback. Built in a weekend, with an editorial look borrowed from fashion magazines. Links: [The map](https://zhouyi-xiaoxiao.github.io/bristol-llm-housing-map/) · [Repository](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/bristol-llm-housing-map) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/workshop/#r-projects_code-bristol-housing-map
- 18 Apr 2026 – 19 Apr 2026 · **Global HackTour London: one city, three cuts** (Global HackTour 伦敦站：一座城，三种剪辑) — Took part. At the in-person Global HackTour London at UCL on 18–19 April 2026, built ‘London Cuts — One City, Three Cuts’: upload a London memory and get back a story in three narrative modes — Punk, Fashion, Cinema — along with a collectible postcard and a pin on a story atlas. The weekend prototype became the London Cuts product. Links: [Repository (London Cuts)](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/london-cuts) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/workshop/#r-ai_research-global-hacktour-london
- 1 Apr 2026 – 8 Apr 2026 · **A route-decision page for a snowy Iceland drive** (为冰岛雪路自驾做的路线决策页) — Completed. In April 2026, a self-drive around Iceland’s ring road, along the south coast and through the East Fjords to Akureyri, with a stop in Oslo. For one snowy leg — Bakkagerði to Akureyri by Route 94, Mývatn, Húsavík and Goðafoss — a public Chinese route-decision site laid out A, B and C options with links to the official road conditions. Planning a trip like a product, again. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/workshop/#r-education_life-iceland-ring-road-2026
- 15 Mar 2026 · **Why the browser’s voice input went deaf** (浏览器的语音输入为什么「聋」了) — Published. A bilingual repository that diagnosed why voice input failed in the ChatGPT Atlas browser — it stored its own audio-input priority and preferred an external monitor’s microphone over the built-in one — and ships an audit script and a reversible fix that reorders the priority, plus a userscript that keeps video speed controls on ordinary sites. Links: [Repository](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/chatgpt-atlas-voice-video-speed-fix) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/workshop/#r-projects_code-atlas-voice-fix
- 7 Mar 2026 – 10 Jun 2026 · **Open-source agent skills** (开源的智能体技能包) — Shipped. A public, sanitised collection of reusable skills and setup kits for coding agents — mail access, security-minded skills and a portable configuration template — plus small utilities for AI desktop apps. The larger personal library stays private; what is published is what anyone can safely reuse. Links: [Skills collection](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/codex-skills-public-collection) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/workshop/#r-ai_research-agent-skills-oss
- 1 Mar 2026 – 9 Mar 2026 · **UK AI Agent Hack at Imperial** (帝国理工 UK AI Agent Hack) — Took part. Took part in the week-long UK AI Agent Hackathon EP4, which opened on 1 March 2026 at Imperial College London — and shared the call with the PhD community of SEMT, the School of Engineering Mathematics and Technology the day before. The entry was SocialOS, submitted to five bounty tracks at once; the public repository keeps the pitch pack, the architecture and the evidence documents. Links: [SocialOS repository](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/openclaw-foundry-socialos) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/workshop/#r-ai_research-uk-ai-agent-hack-socialos
- 17 Feb 2026 – 14 Jul 2026 · **An always-on agent host, deliberately uninstalled** (一台 7×24 在线的智能体主机，用后主动卸载) — Completed. A spare laptop became an always-on host for an open-source autonomous agent framework, driven from a phone through ordinary chat apps to run coding and browser tasks, with multi-agent channels, scheduled digests and an automated development loop for the SocialOS codebase. About two months of real use surfaced where autonomous agents break today: authentication churn, reliability when nobody is watching, and permissions that sprawl. The whole setup was uninstalled in July 2026 — the experiment was the point. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/workshop/#r-ai_research-openclaw-agent-host
- 29 Nov 2024 · **A Tianjin University letterhead in LaTeX** (天津大学公函版式的 LaTeX 模板) — Published. A bilingual XeLaTeX template that reproduces Tianjin University’s letterhead style — TJU blue, a logo slot, a contact block — written during the PhD application season for reference letters, then published so that anyone else applying could use it too. It was announced on LinkedIn twenty-five minutes after the repository was created. On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/workshop/#r-projects_code-tju-letter-template
- 21 Aug 2023 – 22 Aug 2023 · **TJU_Draw: shapes you can drag and rotate** (TJU_Draw：可以拖拽与旋转的图形) — Completed. A Windows drawing application written in C++ with MFC for the Tianjin University School of Mathematics computer practicum: draw lines, circles, ellipses, squares, rectangles and triangles, change stroke and fill colours, then drag, scale and rotate the shapes to any angle. The earliest interactive graphics in this collection — the plate on the home page is a distant descendant. Links: [Repository](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/TJU_Draw) On the site: https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/workshop/#r-projects_code-tju-draw
- 1 Dec 2021 · **Joined GitHub** (开通 GitHub 账号) — Ongoing. The GitHub account dates from 1 December 2021. For three years it was quiet — coursework, a maths guide, a template — and then, in 2026, it erupted: most of the repositories were created that year, along with nearly all of the contributions, including a two-day spike when automated coding agents built a hackathon product. The counts on this page come from GitHub’s public contribution calendar, up to the last day shown under it. Company work in private repositories is not counted, so the graph is a lower bound, not the whole output.
